data.long_meaning: Mangal is a Sanskrit name derived from the word 'Mangalam' which means 'auspiciousness' or 'fortune'. In Hindu mythology, Mangal is the name of a planet, Mars, and the god of war. This name is believed to bring good luck and prosperity. The name Mangal carries the meaning “Auspicious, Fortunate” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Mangal usually hope their child will grow to embody auspicious, fortunate and live with faith, good character and purpose.

The selection of a child's name is based on the position and influence of the stars and planets at the time of their birth. Mangal is believed to be a powerful and fortunate name, and it is often chosen for those born under the influence of Mars.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, the planet Mars is considered to be the god of war, and it is also known as Mangal or Kuja. Mangal is seen as a symbol of energy, courage, and good fortune. The worship of Mangal is believed to bring prosperity, success in battles, protection from harm, and good fortune. The placement of Mars in a person's horoscope is believed to have a significant impact on their personality, inclinations, and future prospects. Mangal is also associated with the god of fertility, and it is believed that the name Mangal can bring blessings of abundance and prosperity in material and spiritual terms.
